union.summary: `wrappedList` violates markdown-it's silent/non-silent block-rule invariant that every paragraph-terminator consumer depends on
union.evidence:
`wrappedList` (packages/notes/src/view/list-empty-bullet-plugin.ts:181-193) returns `true` in silent mode WITHOUT delegating to `originalList`, so it never applies the stock `list` rule's own preconditions — notably markdown-it 14.x list.mjs's `if (state.sCount[startLine] - state.blkIndent >= 4) return false` and the `state.listIndent >= 0 && sCount - listIndent >= 4 && sCount < blkIndent` guard. Every consumer of the `paragraph`/`blockquote`/`reference` terminator chains assumes `silent === true` is a pure predicate: "a block really will start on this line." Those consumers are `markdown-it/lib/rules_block/paragraph.mjs`, `blockquote.mjs`, `reference.mjs`, plus the in-repo copy of that loop at packages/notes/src/view/list-empty-bullet-plugin.ts:119-127 (`terminatorRules[i](state, nextLine, endLine, true)`). Concrete divergence: `isEmptyBulletLine` (line 31-32) only checks `sCount[line] >= blkIndent`, with no 4-space code-block ceiling. For input `foo\n -` (6 spaces), silent mode now returns `true`, the paragraph is cut short, and the non-silent pass reaches that line where the real `list` rule refuses it (indent >= 4) — so the `code` rule claims it and the note renders `

foo

  -
` instead of the previous lazy-continuation `foo
-`. The same shortcut also bypasses the `listIndent` guard for deeply-indented lines inside an existing list item. Fix belongs on the new code: `isEmptyBulletLine` should reproduce the stock rule's indent preconditions, or `wrappedList` should confirm `originalList` would also accept the line non-silently before short-circuiting.

union.summary: Behaviour change to `NotePreview.render` silently re-renders all existing stored notes that use a single-dash setext H2
union.evidence:
The plugin rejects ANY lone single `-` as a setext underline (packages/notes/src/view/list-empty-bullet-plugin.ts:107), not just an indented one under a list item. So a top-level `Title\n-` — a valid CommonMark/GFM H2 — now renders as `

Title

` through packages/notes/src/view/preview.ts:165. The consumer that was not considered is every existing note's stored content: per docs/design/notes/notes.md:243-245 a note's content *is* its raw markdown string in one Yorkie `Text` at `root.content` (see packages/backend/src/yorkie/note-content.ts and packages/frontend/src/app/notes/yorkie-note-store.ts), so there is no versioning or migration step — previously-authored `-` underlines change appearance for all collaborators the moment this ships, and gain a stray empty bullet. The change's own plan listed this case as a required test (`top-level lone dash`, docs/tasks/active/20260724-notes-empty-bullet-setext-todo.md:60) but no such test exists in packages/notes/src/view/preview.test.ts:152-197, and neither the design note (docs/design/notes/notes.md:295-298, which claims only `---`/`=` are affected) nor the user docs mention losing single-dash H2. Fix belongs on the new code: scope `isLoneDash` to lines that are indented relative to the enclosing block, or accept and document the top-level loss.

union.summary: User-facing documentation still claims the notes preview is GitHub-Flavored Markdown, which this change deliberately stops being
union.evidence: packages/documentation/notes/writing-a-note.md:64 states "The preview supports **GitHub-Flavored Markdown** plus a few extras:" and line 71 promises "Links, headings, lists, blockquotes, images — as you'd expect". The diff makes the preview deviate from GFM/cmark-gfm on two documented-by-omission points (a lone `-` is no longer a setext underline; an empty `-`/`*`/`+` bullet now interrupts a paragraph), by the change's own admission in docs/design/notes/notes.md:293-298. This shipped user doc is a consumer of the old contract and was not updated — only the internal design note was. Fix belongs in the documentation file (or in the design note's scope claim).

union.summary: Source pane (`@codemirror/lang-markdown`) still applies CommonMark setext rules, so the default Split view now disagrees with itself
union.evidence: packages/notes/src/view/editor.ts:200 installs `markdown()` from `@codemirror/lang-markdown` (lezer-markdown, CommonMark-compliant), and packages/notes/src/view/editor.ts:117/150 mount the `NotePreview` alongside it. The default view mode is Split (packages/frontend/src/app/notes/notes-toolbar.tsx:48, `{ mode: "both", label: "Split" }`, described as the default in packages/documentation/notes/writing-a-note.md:38). lezer-markdown was not touched by this change, so for `- 1\n  -` (and for `Title\n-`) the editor pane keeps syntax-highlighting the line above as a SetextHeading while the preview pane now renders body text plus a nested empty bullet — the two halves of the same screen show different structure for the same source. Fix belongs in editor.ts (a lezer-markdown config that matches the preview's deviation) or must be accepted and documented as a known split-view mismatch.

union.summary: `getRuleFn`'s private-API `throw` runs at module-import time, so a markdown-it internal rename takes down the whole notes route, not just markdown rendering
union.evidence: `getRuleFn` reads markdown-it's private `__rules__` registry and throws on miss (packages/notes/src/view/list-empty-bullet-plugin.ts:207-213). It is invoked from `listEmptyBulletPlugin` (line 179), which runs at top-level module evaluation of preview.ts (packages/notes/src/view/preview.ts:48). packages/notes/src/view/editor.ts:20 imports `preview.js`, and packages/notes/src/index.ts:12-18 re-exports `initialize` from editor.js — so the throw propagates to import of the entire `@wafflebase/notes` view surface. With `"markdown-it": "^14.1.0"` (packages/notes/package.json:63) a caret-range minor/patch bump that touches the private registry shape would blank the whole notes route (editor, sync, toolbar) rather than degrade one markdown edge case. Fix belongs on the new code: fall back to a no-op wrapper instead of throwing, or pin the dependency.

union.summary: `at('lheading', ...)` omits the `alt` restoration the change's own lessons file says is required
union.evidence: docs/tasks/active/20260724-notes-empty-bullet-setext-lessons.md:18-22 records that `Ruler.at(name, fn, options)` REPLACES the rule's `alt` chain with `options.alt || []`. packages/notes/src/view/list-empty-bullet-plugin.ts:197-199 correctly restores `list`'s `['paragraph','reference','blockquote']`, but line 175 replaces `lheading` with no options at all. Upstream markdown-it 14.x registers `lheading` with no `alt`, so there is no impact today; it only becomes a defect if another plugin (installed before line 175 — e.g. a future katex/details variant) has given `lheading` an alt chain, which `at()` would then silently discard. Defensive only.

union.summary: The `isLoneDash` guard kills *every* single-dash setext heading in the preview, not just indented empty bullets — existing note content using `Title\n-` for an H2 now renders as a paragraph plus a stray empty bullet
union.evidence:
The deviation is not scoped to `state.blkIndent > 0` / inside-a-list context. `lheadingRule` rejects any `-` underline of run length 1 at any nesting level (`list-empty-bullet-plugin.ts:104`), then `wrappedList` (`:183-192`) terminates the paragraph and the stock `list` rule claims the line. So top-level `Title\n-` — a legitimate CommonMark H2 that renders as `

` everywhere else, including the editor pane — now renders `

Title

` in the preview. Note content already stored in Yorkie (`packages/frontend/src/app/notes/yorkie-note-store.ts`) is re-rendered through this single shared `md` instance (`packages/notes/src/view/preview.ts:14,165`), so this is a silent rendering regression for existing documents, not only for the newly-typed shape the issue describes. The diff's tests only cover the multi-dash form (`preview.test.ts:182-187`); the todo listed a "top-level lone dash" case (`docs/tasks/active/20260724-notes-empty-bullet-setext-todo.md:62`) that never landed. Fix belongs in the new plugin: gate the deviation on being inside a list item / non-zero `blkIndent`.

union.summary: `getRuleFn` throws from a module-scope `md.use(...)`, so a markdown-it internals change turns a rendering bug into a hard import-time crash of the whole notes editor
union.evidence: `getRuleFn` reads markdown-it's private `__rules__` registry and `throw new Error(...)` when the name is absent (`list-empty-bullet-plugin.ts:205-213`). It is invoked from `md.use(listEmptyBulletPlugin)` at module top level in `packages/notes/src/view/preview.ts:48`, and `preview.ts` is imported unconditionally by `packages/notes/src/view/editor.ts:20`, which is the package's public `initialize()` export (`packages/notes/src/index.ts:12-18`) consumed by the frontend notes route (`packages/frontend/src/app/notes/notes-view.tsx`). markdown-it is a floating range (`packages/notes/package.json:63`, `"markdown-it": "^14.1.0"`), so if the private registry is ever renamed/reshaped the failure mode is not a mis-rendered bullet but an exception during module evaluation that takes the entire notes editor (and any bundle importing it) down. Prefer a non-throwing fallback (skip the wrap and leave stock `list` in place) over an unhandled module-init throw.

union.summary: The editor pane's markdown grammar was not updated, so the two panes now disagree: CodeMirror highlights `- 1\n  -` / `Title\n-` as a setext heading while the preview renders a bullet
union.evidence: `buildExtensions` installs `markdown()` from `@codemirror/lang-markdown` (`packages/notes/src/view/editor.ts:200`, dep at `packages/notes/package.json:53`), which uses lezer-markdown's strict CommonMark grammar and still parses a lone `-` after a paragraph as a `SetextHeading` underline. The same buffer is rendered side-by-side by `preview.render(currentDoc())` (`editor.ts:150`), which after this change nests it as an empty bullet. In split ('both') mode the user sees heading-styled source next to body-text output for the exact shape issue #517 is about. The plugin deviation is preview-only by design (`docs/design/notes/notes.md:298`), but nothing in the diff records or handles the editor-side inconsistency.

union.summary: The design note describes a narrower contract than the code implements: it claims ordinary setext headings still render and that only `-` is affected, but single-dash setext H2s are dropped everywhere and `*`/`+` empty bullets also gained paragraph-interrupting power
union.evidence:
`docs/design/notes/notes.md:295-298` says "a **lone single `-`** (the empty-bullet shape) is never a setext underline … Multi-dash `---` and `=` setext underlines are untouched, so ordinary setext headings still render." Single-dash `Title
-` *is* an ordinary setext heading and no longer renders as one (see `list-empty-bullet-plugin.ts:104`). Separately, the second relaxation is not dash-only: `isEmptyBulletLine` accepts `-`, `*` and `+` (`list-empty-bullet-plugin.ts:38-40`), so `foo
*` and `foo
+` now also terminate the paragraph and emit an empty list instead of the previous lazy-continuation text — behaviour the doc and the lessons file (`docs/tasks/active/20260724-notes-empty-bullet-setext-lessons.md:9-12`) do not mention.

union.summary: Fragile install-order invariant: the fix silently disappears if any plugin registered after this one touches `list`/`lheading`, and the hardcoded `alt` chain overwrites anything an earlier plugin added to `list`
union.evidence: `listEmptyBulletPlugin` captures the current `list` fn at install time (`list-empty-bullet-plugin.ts:179`) and then hardcodes upstream's chain via `md.block.ruler.at('list', wrappedList, { alt: ['paragraph','reference','blockquote'] })` (`:197-199`). Two out-of-diff hazards: (a) it must be the last `md.use` that touches those two rules — `packages/notes/src/view/preview.ts:36-48` happens to satisfy that today (taskLists is core-only, `detailsPlugin` only sets its own rule's alt at `details-plugin.ts:104-106`), but nothing enforces it, so a future plugin appended after line 48 that replaces `lheading`/`list` reverts #517 with no test failure; (b) any `alt` entry a previously installed plugin (e.g. `@vscode/markdown-it-katex`) or a future markdown-it 14.x release adds to `list` is silently wiped by the hardcoded array. Reading the existing options instead of re-declaring them, plus a comment pinning the ordering requirement at the `md.use` site, would remove both.

union.summary: A verbatim fork of upstream `lheading` is pinned only by a comment while the dependency range floats, so upstream fixes to that rule will silently stop applying to the notes preview
union.evidence: `list-empty-bullet-plugin.ts:67` documents the rule body as a copy of "markdown-it 14.x `rules_block/lheading.mjs`" (including a re-implementation of markdown-it's private `asciiTrim`, `:20-26`), but `packages/notes/package.json:63` declares `"markdown-it": "^14.1.0"`. Any 14.x patch to `lheading` (or to `asciiTrim` semantics) is installed by the lockfile bump yet never reaches the preview, because `md.block.ruler.at('lheading', lheadingRule)` (`:175`) replaces it outright. There is no test asserting fork/upstream parity, so the divergence would be invisible.
